nodeData.topic: Class 5 · Preparing to Enter the Merciful Kartik Month
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Before Kartik 2025, Maharaj explains why it is the best month for advancement and how to offer the lamp to Damodara with eyes and mind fixed on the Lord, not mere waving. He guides devotees to choose their own vows (rounds, bathing, hearing, fasting, avoiding gossip), take a sankalpa praying to Mother Radharani, serve a devotee daily and give a gift at the end. In the Q&A he stresses commitment, real rather than imagined service, outreach with Tulsi-stick lamps, and fasting by a self-designed plan to please Damodara. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj calls Kartik the best month of the year: the best time for prayer, meditation and devotional activity. Everything culminates in Kartik, so any devotee who wants to advance should give this period special attention.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:33 (auto-transcript): “I was saying that this is the best of months. Karthik. Best of the time in the year. The best of the months in the year. The best of activities in the year. The best of prayers in the year. The best meditation in the year. The best memory. Everything everything ends in…”

children.topic: A good time to get serious
children.note:
In Kali-yuga our minds, senses and intelligence are dull under the mode of ignorance. Maharaj cites the Padma Purana: if even an unserious person reaches Krishna's personal service by regulated devotion in Kartik, isn't this the time for us to get serious?

🎙 Maharaj at 12:14 (auto-transcript): “If even an unserious person, unserious person, could applicable to most of us because in Kali Yuga we have dull brain, dull head, dull mind, dull senses, dull intelligence. Everything we do is full of dullness because we are predominated by the mode of ignorance. The mode of…”

What Kartik offers is great: the Puranas say a lamp offered to Damodara in this month destroys the sins of countless births in an instant. Maharaj adds that even seeing someone offer a lamp brings Krishna's mercy, and lighting a lamp for another to offer, and offering oneself, frees one from rebirth. — “What is available is great.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:53 (auto-transcript): “Because of what is available. What is available is great. So great that when one offers a lamb during the month of Karthik, His sins of many thousands and millions of birds perish in half an eye blink. Millions of sins they won't commit. For sin sign in memory can be terminated.”

Simply waving a lamp is not Damodara's offering. Maharaj asks us to recognise we are offering to a person and to see Damodara with both eyes and mind, then offer carefully: four times to the lotus feet, two to the navel, three to the face and seven to the whole body. The benefit cannot be calculated. — “I am doing this for a person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:11 (auto-transcript): “But I'm telling you, I'm telling you, waving lamb, that is not Damodara's offering. It should be done with concentration. We should recognize that I am doing this for a person. I should see that person. That means we should see the Damodara. We should see him both ways. both…”

For years Maharaj has watched crowds in Vrindavan wave lamps in every direction with no concentration, so he avoids crowded offerings. By Kartik's glory Damodara still accepts, but that is no reason not to do it properly. — “someone almost burnt my ear”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:05 (auto-transcript): “I've seen many times for many years how people offer the lamp in Brindavan someone almost burnt my ear in Brindavan So I don't go to a heavy crowded place for opening, no concentration, no concentration for the people and you yourself, no concentration. Everybody is waving,…”

In Lagos Maharaj has devotees sit quietly and all recite the prayers attentively first, then offer the lamp with full concentration. Out of dullness we often do not even look at the One we offer to, do not join the singing, or sing only for pride.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:54 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, to help devotees facilitate this, maximize this benefit, I used to tell devotees, let us sit down quietly, attentively, recite the prayers first with full concentration. Everybody should participate to recite the prayers fully. Then we can do the second thing, open…”

A Puranic verse says one's ancestors are liberated when a family member offers Keshava a lamp, by the mercy of the Lord who holds the Sudarshan chakra. Maharaj unpacks the name: su-darshan is the most auspicious sight of the Lord, and the chakra destroys, so true darshan destroys our sins. — “To see Lord Krishna is very, very auspicious.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:28 (auto-transcript): “Let us look at it, sudarsan, and then chakra. Sudarsan, sudarsan. Sudarsan means that we are having the vision. We are seeing. It is su, su, very, very auspicious. To see Lord Krishna is very, very auspicious. And more auspicious is that chakra. Chakra does what? Chakra has…”

children.topic: A gold ring and its stone
children.note:
Darshan is not only admiring the deity's outfit, though appreciating the pujari's devotion is good. A gold ring is complete, but set with a precious stone it becomes far more valuable; darshan with the prayer that the Lord remove all inauspiciousness changes everything in the same way.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:25 (auto-transcript): “Let me have darshan of the Lord, darshan. It's not to see the zeal. the deity put on that day. In order to appreciate the experience, it's good. It's good to appreciate the experience of the pujari, the bhav, the pujari has put into his or her service to the Lord. It's good.…”

Fortunate devotees take full advantage of Kartik and set aside their worries, which the mode of ignorance puts on us. Concentrating on the Lord's darshan, we let him destroy our so-called worries and imperfections and give the lasting blessing of pure love and service.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:42 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, fortunate devotees who take full advantage of this period abandon all our worries about whatever varieties of worries you have. That will just keep them aside. They have nothing to do with us. The worries, everything we have has nothing to do with us. But…”

For Kartik, Maharaj lists daily essentials: bathe every morning whatever the weather, wear fresh clothes, rise early for japa, and increase one's rounds. Asked later about timing, he says bathe whenever you get up, then begin.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:29 (auto-transcript): “so this this period we should try to do certain things for those of us who are not living in the temple and and for those of us who live in the temple i must bet every morning compulsorily. I must bet every morning compulsorily. Either it is winter and sick. Whatever the…”

No one should impose a number of rounds: 20, 25, 32, 50, 64 or 108, each devotee decides. Once decided, make a sankalpa by praying to the acharyas and Srimati Radharani.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:29 (auto-transcript): “I must increase. I must increase the number. And nobody should impose any number. You should decide. I can do with 20. I can do with 25. I can do with 32. I can do with 34. I can do with 50. I can do with 64. I can do with 108. You should decide. We should decide. And when it…”

Maharaj gives a prayer: a mother does not count her baby's offences, even when it wets or kicks her, so please do not reject me; keep me tied to your lotus feet so I keep my vows and become a good devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:23 (auto-transcript): “And we should offer this prayer. My dear mother, Yes, order, Maria, Sumatya Radharani. A mother never considered the offenses of the children. So please, don't take my offenses seriously. Don't reject me. Please maintain me even though I pass water on your body. I kick you…”

Choose in advance what to hear and chant daily: Bhagavatam, a Gita chapter, Sri Radha Kripa Kataksha Stotra, acharyas' ashtakas to Radharani. Food vows such as no grains or one meal a day are chosen too; these acts can be done any time, but in Kartik they are different, as a deity worshipped daily is specially present on its appearance day.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:47 (auto-transcript): “As you hear Bhagavatam, or as you hear Bhagavad Gita, a chapter, or some bhajans, which we keep, and Sissi Radha, Kripa, Kataksa, Krishna, Stotra, We want to hear this regularly, every day. And some other bhajans and other asakam of our acharyas for Sumatera Dharani, we want…”

Alongside what we will do, decide what we will not do: speaking badly about anyone, gossip of every kind and idle talk. Married couples abstain from sex, and many give up sweets and sugar. Use the time to talk and hear about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:36 (auto-transcript): “and we should also have the things we shouldn't do for these people so they do or they don't I'm going to hear Krishna, I'm going to hear Bajan I'm going to hear narrations I'm going to try to avoid try to avoid talking bad about people so try to avoid talking bad about…”

Someone told Maharaj that every festival is about fasting and he would rather feast. Maharaj lets him, but says the better way is to sacrifice now as preparation, because in Goloka there is no fasting, only an eternal feast. — “There's no fasting in Goloka.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:03 (auto-transcript): “too dry. One day what he told me, Mahara, you know, all our festival is about fasting, fasting. I don't want to take away in the country because the only festival which was not fasting God and Prussia I don't want to fast so I can feast that's okay if I would okay you can do…”

Take a vow to do something for a devotee each day, even a small thing or a gift. — “Before a day passes, I must do something to help a devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:49 (auto-transcript): “Take a vow that I must try to do good things for devotees. At least one day I must do something. One day I must do something. Before a day passes, I must do something to help a devotee. Something. and they call it what you seek or do something, give a gift. And at the…”

At the end of Kartik it is compulsory to give a gift and, for householders, to feed devotees; this offsets mistakes made through inattention and dullness, and the more advanced the devotee, the better. If no devotees live nearby, keep an item each day and give thirty at the month's end.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:14 (auto-transcript): “And at the completion of our critique, it is compulsory for us to give a gift. It is compulsory to give a gift, somebody. To, as householders, feed a gift to Brahman. That will nullify some mistakes which we made accidentally or unintentionally or due to inattentiveness, due…”

After reading from The Nectar of Devotion about worshipping Damodara, Maharaj explains that pilgrimage, sacrifice, full-moon charity and new-moon fasting all culminate in Kartik, the final stop for every pious act. He asks each devotee to make Kartik 2025 the best of their life. — “everything ends here”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:48 (auto-transcript): “So many quotations from the Purana. Prophet Putin is next to the devotion. In this month, all the activities which we do for either Kuskara or Kursetra or Holy Sacrifice or the Full Moon Charity or the New Moon Fasting, everything, everything that we do other times, they…”

Devotees ask about the lamp offering, vows and service.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:38 (auto-transcript): “Gurudev, I have a peculiar problem. You started saying that, you know, when we do the lamp offering, you need to have a full concentration of mind and eyes. But my problem is when I'm concentrating, I'm concentrating more on the number of offerings and rounds that we have to…”

While offering the lamp, a devotee finds himself concentrating on counting the circles rather than on the deity.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:38 (auto-transcript): “Gurudev, I have a peculiar problem. You started saying that, you know, when we do the lamp offering, you need to have a full concentration of mind and eyes. But my problem is when I'm concentrating, I'm concentrating more on the number of offerings and rounds that we have to…”

Looking at the feet while counting four is itself meditation and helps focus; if the mind is not on the Lord's form it will wander elsewhere. — “So look at the feet and count.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:13 (auto-transcript): “Well, if you are offering four to the feet, so you are looking at the feet. But I'm counting. Oh, is it four? Is it three? It's okay. You're counting. Yes, you're counting, but you're looking at the feet. So look at the feet and count. That is meditation. It is called Ruk…”

Afraid of breaking a month-long vow, a mataji asks whether occasional extra rounds or austerities without a vow still count.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:30 (auto-transcript): “a person like me couldn't take much of the vows for the entire month but sometimes like it's not like I couldn't take but out of the fear that it will broke so is it correct to do austerity like odd number of days that you try maximum number of rounds more that will be…”

Taking a vow makes it serious and committed; changing the number from day to day makes practice random, not regulated.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:05 (auto-transcript): “if you take the vow, make it serious if you take the vow I'm going to do 22 if you take the vow or I'm going to do 18 if you take the vow, then it becomes serious otherwise, okay I will do I told you I would do 18 to mark and do 20 and do 16 to that day. Then it means no…”

If one cannot help a devotee on some day, is praying for them mentally enough?

🎙 Maharaj at 54:10 (auto-transcript): “My question is that you told we should try to do something to help a devotee daily. So if any day if we don't get chance can we pray mentally for them? Well, we yes, I know I know that in this material world there is always a chance for mistake and take but we should not be…”

Do not plan around failure. A hungry belly is not filled by meditating on food; plan something real, like calling and greeting a devotee. — “you should make it real”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:27 (auto-transcript): “Well, we yes, I know I know that in this material world there is always a chance for mistake and take but we should not be meditating on mistakes. we shouldn't be meditating on that let us plan I want to maybe call a devotee and greet okay today I'm not able to I just…”

children.topic: Q4 · Empower me to rise early
children.note:
A mataji confesses laziness and asks Maharaj to empower her to rise early and chant sixteen rounds in Kartik.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:01 (auto-transcript): “I want to pray to you please empower me that in this Karthik month I get up early and do 16 rounds only I know you always empower me I am only lazy I am not only able to do it but please pray for me and please empower me for this getting up early in the morning ok thank you I…”

Maharaj promises to come and knock on her door, on one condition: once woken, she must not go back to sleep. — “I'm going to knock on your door.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:30 (auto-transcript): “I will come to your house I'll knock on your door. Don't worry. I'm going to knock on your door. Are you ready? I'll wake you. Yeah. Please empower me. Please come in. If I wake you, if I wake you, you should not sleep again. I won't sleep again. Okay. Okay. I will come.…”

Can lamps made with Tulsi sticks be offered to Damodara, and is there extra benefit?

🎙 Maharaj at 62:51 (auto-transcript): “So both of them are asking that can we offer Tulsi stick lamp to Damodar and is there any extra benefit of doing that? Yes, it is a standard Lagos standpoint. We only offer Tulsi stick. And Tulsi is so suspicious, it's in the Padma Purana, Skanda Purana, it is mentioned…”

In Lagos only Tulsi sticks are used; the Puranas say a sacrifice with a Tulsi stick has incalculable merit, all the more when offered to Krishna. When you find something good, share it, and give guests sticks too. — “You are expanding their fortune.”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:02 (auto-transcript): “Yes, it is a standard Lagos standpoint. We only offer Tulsi stick. And Tulsi is so suspicious, it's in the Padma Purana, Skanda Purana, it is mentioned there. Any Jagia which we do, and the Tulsi stick is offered there, there is no calculation to the merit of that Jagia.”

Further questions, mostly on fasting and inviting others.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:24 (auto-transcript): “how should we maintain the fast and diet which is to be followed in the Dhamudar month how do we get the determination to maintain the fast and the diet that we decide to take up? Determination will come from understanding what is the purpose of fasting? Why am I doing this?…”

children.topic: Q6 · Determination to keep the fast
children.note:
How do we find the determination to keep the fast and diet we choose?

🎙 Maharaj at 65:24 (auto-transcript): “how should we maintain the fast and diet which is to be followed in the Dhamudar month how do we get the determination to maintain the fast and the diet that we decide to take up? Determination will come from understanding what is the purpose of fasting? Why am I doing this?…”

Determination comes from understanding why we fast and what we hope to achieve; if the goal matters, we put our full effort in. Srila Prabhupada wrote all this in The Nectar of Devotion because he knew it was good for us.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:40 (auto-transcript): “Determination will come from understanding what is the purpose of fasting? Why am I doing this? What do I help to achieve? What is the purpose? If you don't have a purpose for what we do, we cannot put our best into it. If we don't understand what we are doing, we cannot put…”

Is it necessary to call new people for the lamp offering?

🎙 Maharaj at 67:38 (auto-transcript): “is it necessary to call new people for Deept Dhani yes every day you should do that I know one friend in Dubai her name is Madhuri Lila as they say, Kattu, Pahus, the disciples, even Dubai. For the whole of this month, she take a vow and will visit 350 houses for this month.…”

Yes, every day. Maharaj tells of a devotee in Dubai who vowed to visit hundreds of homes in one Kartik, carrying lamps and showing families how to offer late into the night. This is Krishna consciousness; we expand by bringing new people. — “This is how we expand.”

🎙 Maharaj at 67:43 (auto-transcript): “yes every day you should do that I know one friend in Dubai her name is Madhuri Lila as they say, Kattu, Pahus, the disciples, even Dubai. For the whole of this month, she take a vow and will visit 350 houses for this month. Introduce the Dhammadara offering to her. Every day…”

Devotees feel ashamed comparing their austerities with those of the parampara's acharyas.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:10 (auto-transcript): “A lot of questions are on the theme of fasting and austerities. So, like, Ragini Mataji was asking, how should we take food stuff and Charan Padma Mataji did not understand the importance of fasting in Karthik. Similarly, Gurdayanath Prabhu is asking, when we think about…”

Raghunatha dasa Goswami threw away his cup when a servant replaced it with a bigger one. We need not fast like that; design your own plan, one meal a day, or two without grains, and keep to it. — “You know, it shouldn't be an imposition.”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:42 (auto-transcript): “We don't have to fight the way our acharyas did because Rabbi Nadej Goswami was drinking Potamig, one cup. And one day, When his servant went and changed the cup, he got a bigger cup and pulled the milk there. When Raghuram Dalai Goswami came in, when he saw that, he said,…”

A mataji is still unclear why she should fast in Kartik and what she will gain.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:04 (auto-transcript): “I am still not clear on the importance of fasting during Karthik, my mind is still thinking, why should I fast? What will I get? You should fight because you want to please Lord Damodara so that he can bless you with tickets to go back to Godhead. You see what you say here?…”

We fast to please Lord Damodara so he blesses us with a ticket back to Godhead, where service is pure and unmixed.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:15 (auto-transcript): “You should fight because you want to please Lord Damodara so that he can bless you with tickets to go back to Godhead. You see what you say here? No. So, I want to please Lord Damodara so he'll give me tickets to go back to Godhead. There I will serve him purely not mixed…”

As with Ekadashi, does a stricter Kartik fast bring greater benefit?

🎙 Maharaj at 73:56 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Srila Gurudev, I have a question myself around the fasting. So on Ekadashi, we were hearing you mentioned that when one does nirjal, one gets 100%. When one takes something, fruits or something, it's just 70% and if we eat then it is just 50%. So similarly even…”

Results do differ: one meal a day cannot be equated with two meals without grains, or with no vow at all. But don't jump to someone else's height; do what you can now and rise step by step.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:42 (auto-transcript): “if a person who decided, I will take one meal a day, we cannot equate the result of it with the person who is eating two times a day. But no grain, but I'm eating two times a day. We cannot equate it. Because it's more serious. If equate it means that Krishna is special. You…”

nodeData.topic: Class 4 · Pride Is the Root Cause of Conflict
nodeData.note: SB 6.7.16–6.8.42 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Reading the end of Indra's offence to Brihaspati and the Narayana-kavaca, Maharaj shows how pride and familiarity make us neglect the guru, and how an offence follows us wherever we go, while sincere service makes everything easy. He explains the power of obeisances, why we should respect everyone since we cannot see who is a pure devotee, Vishvarupa's humility in accepting service, and how Lord Vishnu protects devotees who stay within their principles. Questions cover a guru's burden for disciples, Sukracharya's power, curses, sleep, and using the Narayana-kavaca for bhakti. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Indra realises his mistake and repents openly in his own assembly, which Maharaj calls very difficult and very good, since the fire of repentance bends reactions. Still, Brihaspati disappears so that the offence bears fruit and teaches everyone never to disrespect the guru. — “Repentance, the fire of repentance, very, very powerful.”

Recalling Bhaktivinoda Thakura's Saranagati, Maharaj asks where our fortune is found: with devotees, and the guru is the best devotee. We did not merit our fortune; he caused it, so when he is displeased, peace goes and only anxiety remains. — “Spiritual master is our fortune.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:07 (auto-transcript): “Shalabhakti Nautakura said in Saranagati, our fortune is found. Where do we find our fortune? Where do we find our fortune? Our fortune is with devotees. Yes, that is why we find our fortune. So the spiritual master, for us is the best devotee. So, Indra is saying here, alas,…”

children.topic: An offence follows wherever you run
children.note:
Maharaj tells of a great speaker on whose tongue Saraswati lived, who offended a Vaishnavi and lost everything: he became a speculator, fell ill, and wherever he fled, the news arrived first. A song says that the contaminated person who runs to the sea finds it boiling. But with the guru's blessing, as Prabhupada writes in the Gita purports, all principles become easy to follow; a mistake is forgivable, an offence is dangerous.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:06 (auto-transcript): “This is what happened to our life. When Rupa Kaviraj offended Krishna Priya Takurani, although he Saraswati lives on his tongue, Saraswati speaks to him. When he speaks, his tone will melt. When he speaks, because Saraswati was liberty. But when he offended Krishna Priya…”

Brahma rebukes the demigods: because Brihaspati came every day, they took him for granted and thought one morning's obeisances were enough. Maharaj uses this to examine what our own daily obeisances mean.

A senior godbrother who served Prabhupada's meals offered obeisances each time he left and each time he returned with a chapati. He wondered whether Prabhupada would tell him to stop, but Prabhupada never did, and he understood this is how it should be done.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:10 (auto-transcript): “We were serving in the power party for years. He mentioned, which was what we met when we came to the movement. This is different, but what we met was different. So he was telling us how, when he, in the course of his service to the Prabhupada, see, he observed, when he's…”

Maharaj asks the class, and devotees answer: gratitude to the guru, showing submission, reducing false ego, destroying sins, pleasing the Lord, ceasing to see the guru as ordinary, and becoming obedient again after disobeying Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:41 (auto-transcript): “Why do we have to pay obeisances? Why? What is there in obeisances? Why do we have to pay obeisances? Is it not false to God? You're sitting there in obeisances? What is it? What is it in obeisances? Grateful to a guru? Or one paying obeisances? Who? You are grateful to him.…”

In the Caitanya-caritamrta, Mahaprabhu takes sannyasa so that those offending him will offer obeisances and be freed of sin. Obeisances are for our benefit, not the guru's. Every acharya's writing begins with obeisances, glorification and invoking blessings, because without them nothing wonderful can be done.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:12 (auto-transcript): “In Chaitanya Tamrita, it is mentioned, Krishna Dasgavara Goswami, the chapter dealing with Chaitanya taking sanyas. Chaitanya taking sanyas. The reason why he took sanyas. Christian, as Kabbalah Goswami mentioned, open obeisances destroy our sins. That is why we put…”

The Bhagavatam says the acharya should never be envied as an ordinary man, and the Padma Purana condemns that vision. Maharaj observes that we often honour ordinary people and neglect pure devotees, so the safe course is to respect everyone.

children.topic: Mistaking a pure devotee is our fault
children.note:
Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati taught that if we take a pure devotee for ordinary, the fault is ours. If we serve sincerely, Krishna Himself reveals who is a pure devotee. — “if we mistook a pure devotee for ordinary person,”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:01 (auto-transcript): “Sala Bhaktisana Satswati Takola, he said, 64 principles for community. One of the 64 principles, he said, if we mistook a pure devotee for ordinary person, it's our fault. If we mistook a pure devotee for ordinary person, it's our fault. Ordinary person and pure devotee is…”

children.topic: Not by village or favourite food
children.note:
Maharaj mocks our tests: same village, same food, doesn't correct me, so he must be pure. Blessings given to someone unqualified are checked by Krishna, so sincerity, not artificial humility, is the qualification for receiving what is beyond us.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:54 (auto-transcript): “You don't know how to speculate. because this person from my my village so you are pure devotee you are not my village no you are not yes yes yes you like the same food i eat you're a pure devotee you don't charge me you're a pure devotee you charge us no you're not a pure…”

The demigods, who always defeated the demons, now lose because they offended their guru, while the demons grow strong enough to threaten Brahma's abode by serving Sukracharya. Faith in brahmanas, cows and Govinda keeps one strong; neglect leaves no future.

The prayer that by the guru's mercy the dumb speak and the lame cross mountains shows that the guru gives the potency to transcend the modes of nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:00 (auto-transcript): “A lame man can climb mountain. A blind can see. Dumb can. Yes, yes, yes. Yes, yes, yes. Yes, yes, yes. Why? A special master. A special master. He gives the potency. the spiritual master gives potency for us to transcend the mood of nature for us to be able to do or become…”

Neither money nor scholarship pleases the guru, only sincere service, meaning service without expectation, just to please him. Then everything becomes easy. — “Service without expectation.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:53 (auto-transcript): “We cannot please him by other means. By money, by scholarship. No. Sensei service. What is sensei service? What is sensei service? Sensei service. Service without expectation. No expectation. Only to please him. That is sensei service. Only to please him. Then we won't become…”

A devotee meets danger only by stepping outside his principles. Seeing with the eye of scripture, we are never bewildered. — “A devotee will have problems only when we step outside our principle.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:36 (auto-transcript): “We are fully protected in Christian consciousness. Do you not? We are fully protected. Fully protected. A devotee will have problems only when we step outside our principle. Do you not know? Only when we step out, if you remain within, there is no danger. There is no danger.…”

Why be surprised when someone falls? It happened long ago and only shows today: coming to class only to speak, to mangala-arati only to lead, the japa bag left hanging, giving one's own interpretation. We miss the signs because we are not practising nicely. — “It's a ceremony, not a spiritual discipline.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:49 (auto-transcript): “People get bewildered. Ah, he fell down. Ah, you are a fool. You are a fool. Why? Why are you surprised? For a person to fall today, the person has fallen a long time back, not today. How? How? How? How do you see? A person who has fallen today has fallen long time back, not…”

Brahma sends the demigods to Vishvarupa and openly warns them of his leaning toward the demons. Maharaj calls this a perfect teacher: showing the way to the goal while honestly naming the defect, with no deceit.

Vishvarupa was junior in family, yet his austerities made him powerful enough to protect the demigods. Whatever our caste or situation, practice elevates us. — “anyone can become a true devotee”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:51 (auto-transcript): “Another point here is that Bisharup is inferior to the demigods, but why he was selected? This mic can come out properly. But his penances is a powerful Brahmana. Powerful Brahmana. Why is he a superpower? Yes, why is he a superpower? Because his penances and austerity. Yes,…”

Seniority comes by age or by knowledge: Sukadeva Gosvami spoke the Bhagavatam with his father and elders present because he was appointed. When Mahaprabhu asked Haridasa Thakura to speak on the holy name, Haridasa neither refused out of false humility nor became proud; Maharaj urges seeing things as they are, not externally.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:14 (auto-transcript): “there are two ways we have a certain seniority. Seniority by age. Like Sonakarisi was by age. We also have seniority, which is not by material age, but by the quality of one's knowledge. Like Sukadegu Swami, when he was speaking, his father was present. not only his father…”

Vishvarupa accepts the priesthood saying he must agree for his own benefit. Maharaj calls this bona fide humility: a service that came unasked should be accepted as purification, obeying superiors. — “This is true humility.”

A true brahmana lives simply on gleaned grain and uses gifts only for the Lord. Devotees collect donations for the movement; once personal interest enters, it becomes business and contamination instead of devotional service. — “We are collecting for the movement, not for ourselves.”

🎙 Maharaj at 69:19 (auto-transcript): “This is our qualification to collect the nations. This is our qualification. We are collecting for the movement, not for ourselves. If our personal interest comes in, it is no more devotional service. It is business and it is contamination. The devotional service brings…”

Vishvarupa serves with an undivided mind as purohita, the family's well-wisher. Maharaj adds that a guru's first duty is the welfare of his disciples, and he is happy when he sees them progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:55 (auto-transcript): “The guru's duty is to see the welfare of the disciples. It's a guru's duty. This is his first duty to see that the disciples are benefiting. Then he will be happy when you see the progress of the disciples. He will be happy. 39. The opulence of the demons who are generally…”
Vishvarupa takes the demons' opulence back for Indra through a Vishnu prayer. To oppose Vaishnavas, the demons worship other gods; the strain continues today.

Maharaj mentions temples in the south where Vishnu is put at the back, and Ramanuja having to leave Srirangam for Melkote under threat.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:23 (auto-transcript): “and in in south you see lord shiva temple they pull the vision at the back of the the temple, the altar. So she was in the front here. It's at the back. He pulled out the vision. Which is very, very, very offensive. The battle had been going since time. Ramanuja Shira…”

Krishna's promise in the Gita that His devotee never perishes does not mean devotees have no problems; they are simply never defeated, because Vishnu protects them. — “Devotees will have problems, but they will not be defeated.”
Chapter 8 gives the armour Vishvarupa teaches Indra. Maharaj notes that a devotee in trouble turns to Vishnu, while others go to Shiva, Brahma or Durga.

Placing the syllables forward and then in reverse first purifies, then blocks obstacles, since the demons know you are acting against them and will try to disturb you.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:21 (auto-transcript): “respective. All right, so it is clockwise and anticlockwise. What does that mean? What does that mean? Clockwise and anticlockwise. It means what? What does it signify? It's to remove obstacles. There are more obstacles. First is for purification. The anti-clockwise is to…”

As the prayers begin, Maharaj asks everyone to follow them in the mind as a meditation so the mantra is installed in us. He highlights the prayers for protection from pride and from falling away from bhakti: many have left, but one who prays daily to keep his bhakti will remain. — “we should follow it in the mind”

🎙 Maharaj at 100:15 (auto-transcript): “Now we are getting the mantra. From now onward, you are fully. Yes. this is a meditation as we are reading we should follow it we should follow it in the mind we should follow it not just reading let us follow it if you want the mantra to be installed in us we should follow…”

Commenting on the prayer to Balarama against envious serpents, Maharaj admits that devotees envy each other too, and asks us to pray for protection from both our own envy and that of others. — “Among ourselves, we are very envious.”

🎙 Maharaj at 107:04 (auto-transcript): “Even among us, we are envious of each other. Even among us. Not even outside. Among ourselves, we are very envious. So we should beg Lord Bhagavatam to protect us from envy. Our personal envy and the envies of other people. Next. May the personality of Godhead in his…”

Devotees ask about the verses and about practice.

🎙 Maharaj at 126:01 (auto-transcript): “That's Sloka number 35. 35. 6.7.35. In the first line of the translation, Sri Visurupa said, O demigods, although the acceptance of priesthood is decried as causing the loss of previously acquired brahmanical power. Explain this line for us. 35. 7th chapter. 7th chapter. 7th…”

A devotee asks Maharaj to explain how accepting priesthood loses brahminical power (6.7.35).

🎙 Maharaj at 126:01 (auto-transcript): “That's Sloka number 35. 35. 6.7.35. In the first line of the translation, Sri Visurupa said, O demigods, although the acceptance of priesthood is decried as causing the loss of previously acquired brahmanical power. Explain this line for us. 35. 7th chapter. 7th chapter. 7th…”

If disciples do not practise, the guru takes some of their reactions, so in Vedic culture teachers took very few disciples. Maharaj cites Prabhupada saying a guru may suffer for disciples' activities yet takes the risk, and explains why the initiating guru is most responsible, so the guru is always concerned that disciples follow.

🎙 Maharaj at 128:40 (auto-transcript): “the power is diminished it is said the brahmanical power is it that disciple if they don't practice properly or if the guru if somebody is becoming guru only their power will be diminished if the disciple did not practice properly the guru will not fall down but he will have…”

Sukracharya did not teach surrender to Vishnu, so how did worshipping him make the demons powerful?

🎙 Maharaj at 132:01 (auto-transcript): “Demons became powerful by worshipping Sukracharya, their Guru. But Sukracharya, is he teaching them to surrender to Vishnu or is Kulaguru, what we hear is is Kulaguru not like teaching them more to surrender to Vishnu. So how they became powerful by worshipping such Kulaguru,…”

He taught them their own duties and had mystic power, showing the potency of a guru's position even without pure devotion. Maharaj respects him for declaring in the Eighth Canto that chanting Hare Krishna perfects every ritual mistake, yet he is not a bona fide guru of bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 132:44 (auto-transcript): “Although he's not teaching them devotional service, he has power. He's teaching them their own scriptures, he's teaching them their own mentality, their own duty. He's, he's, he's a guru. she has mystic power and with that he is supporting them and he's also showing us the…”

A devotee notes that many personalities in scripture curse others, even non-devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 135:41 (auto-transcript): “In the same sense, in scriptures, we see many places, many times the demons or other personalities, they give curse, like the grandsons of the grand. You will be killed by your father, call a name in the next life. So, we see many personalities give curse to others. Yes, even…”

As parts of Krishna everyone carries some potency, especially parents. Maharaj recalls his farmer father telling the fussy child he would one day buy that food in the city, and he did, with money.

🎙 Maharaj at 136:11 (auto-transcript): “Yes, even if you are no devotee, if they curse you, you have effect because we are all part and parcel of Krishna. All of us, we are Krishna's part and parcel. Some power is there. So if they If they say something, even our parents, if they consider it, it will have effect.…”

How does Maharaj manage on two or three hours of sleep, when the questioner feels unable to serve without full rest?

🎙 Maharaj at 137:54 (auto-transcript): “you told in the first class that austerity means how one eat, how one speak and how much one sleep. So that part that how much one sleep, like in my case, I feel that if I don't sleep in the recommended quota or something, I feel kind of that I have to sleep otherwise I…”

Such things come with progress; the mind insists we will fall sick while the person beside us sleeps five hours and is fine. A strong mind strengthens the body and the soul controls the senses as practice matures. Like a company doing yearly stock-taking, devotees should check the quality of their practice. — “Mostly, our mind is the problem, the mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 138:43 (auto-transcript): “krishna consciousness that certain things that will come as you are progressing as you are are progressing, these things, they will come. And so this also depends on our mind. Mostly, our mind is the problem, the mind. The mind tells us that if you don't sleep for 10 hours,…”

Indra used the Narayana-kavaca to enjoy heaven; is that a proper use?

🎙 Maharaj at 143:03 (auto-transcript): “here Indra is using this Narayana coverage for sense gratification not for pleasing Krishna or something and here Vishwarup is also teaching for that only to enjoy sense gratification peacefully so is it a proper way we can use it not for same gratification see the whole…”

Use it to control the senses, protect bhakti and overcome envy, just as we fast on Ekadasi for Krishna, not for heaven. Maharaj recites some of these mantras daily, including the one for lust, and urges learning mantras by heart, as Gajendra remembered his.

🎙 Maharaj at 143:31 (auto-transcript): “so is it a proper way we can use it not for same gratification see the whole mantra is very powerful for helping or control our senses helping culture our bhakti helping our envy personal envy and others envies we can use it for ourselves let us not use use the way indra use…”

nodeData.topic: Class 3 · Easy-going Life Means No Advancement
nodeData.note: SB 6.5.31–6.7.15 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Narada's merciful glance delivers Daksha's second group of sons, but Daksha, blind to real success, curses him; Maharaj shows how a devotee answers insult with tolerance, changes the heart rather than the dress, and accepts that an easy-going life means no advancement. After Daksha's sixty daughters and the moon's curse, Indra's pride before Brihaspati shows how opulence steals intelligence and why the guru must be respected without duplicity, while leaders without Krishna steer stone boats. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Narada's glance is never wasted. Maharaj says a devotee should be like this: looking at everyone with a good heart, happy to see other devotees, so that his very presence brings fortune; the Savalasvas were won by Narada's sweetness, not only his words. — “Our presence will create fortune for others.”
The verse compares the departed sons to nights that pass and never come back. Maharaj loves the image: our goal is to go back to Godhead and never return here.

Maharaj tests the idea that a bereaved person is ripe for bhakti. Only a pious soul will take it; Daksha, angry and not pious, could not be delivered even though Narada came personally, after delivering whole families before.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:22 (auto-transcript): “Is it true? Is it true? Are you sure? This is true? If you preach to every person who is bereaved now, they become devotees. If you preach to a bereaved person, they will become devotees. Thank you. Thank you. Only if they are pious, not just anybody, only a pious person will…”

Success means different things: money for the materialist, a big temple and many facilities for an ordinary devotee. Maharaj says fame, followers and facilities can all be failures; the only real success is going back home, back to Godhead. — “Is going back home, back to Godhead.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:01 (auto-transcript): “the success it means different things for different people for a matrilistic person success means what he has money what my life is successful means he has money For a devotee, for a devotee, normal devotee, normal devotee, success means what? I have thousands of devotees in…”

We say we are fine while the heart is full of anxiety. Maharaj says fine means chanting sixteen rounds nicely, appreciating our fortune and wasting no time on unnecessary things; not just 'I'm not in hospital and I slept well'. — “How am I closer to Krishna?”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:48 (auto-transcript): “Fine means that I have chanted my sister around nicely as Rupa Goswami said. That is fine. I have chanted my sister around nicely. and I'm appreciating my Krishna consciousness the fortune has created for me I'm appreciating that and I'm engaging myself in Krishna…”

Daksha calls Narada a false saint and claims to be the better man as an honest householder. Maharaj notes that this boast and fault-finding are signs he is not a devotee, though he was great enough to see Lord Vishnu.

Maharaj asks the class what a perfect householder does: honour and care for brahmacaris, sannyasis and brahmanas, and help dependents get free from birth and death. Daksha does neither; he only trains his sons to enjoy the senses like himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:23 (auto-transcript): “What is household of perfect duty? Because they die. Very good. To honor renounce order of life. To honor renounce order of life. Brahmacharis, sannyasis. Very good. To take care of sannyasis, brahmacharis and brahmanas. Is Daksa doing that? No. to liberate his dependence…”

Our duty, like Narada's, is to show people the path of renouncing this world and going home to Godhead. Maharaj says the best way is personal example, not just words; a sannyasi's begging is really a pretext to preach, and a devotee always asks where he can serve. — “By our personal example.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:10 (auto-transcript): “Our duty is, what is our duty? To show people the path of renunciation. What's the best way to do that? What's the best way to do that? By our personal example. By our personal example. That has to do it. Not just by our words. Our personal example. They will show everyone…”

Daksha says the boys were too inexperienced. Maharaj points out neither route is a guarantee: some enjoyed and still returned to it, others never enjoyed and went back out of curiosity. First-class intelligence is to hear, understand and follow bona fide authority, like the Savalasvas.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:39 (auto-transcript): “not a guarantee it's not a guarantee because we have seen so many people who have had material experience gratified their senses and gave it up after some time they went back to it we have seen many yes this is not a guarantee what is a guarantee what is a guarantee we have…”

The sons were gentle, well behaved and practised austerity nicely, so they followed the order and were purified. Maharaj says if one is convinced of the goal and follows the process strictly, past experience does not matter; and young people who joined immediately have made no mistake. — “Either we have experienced it before or not.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:07 (auto-transcript): “back right they didn't come back so what is the qualification their qualification was due to the quality of their practice they have practiced very very nice austerity and it was mentioned that they were very gentle and well behaved people they were gentle and well behaved…”

Daksha says his sons still owed debts to sages, demigods and father; Maharaj adds we owe our country too. The Bhagavatam's answer is that full surrender to Mukunda clears every debt; Maharaj compares it to a supermarket where everything is bought in one place, and says we need not wait for ordinary people's appreciation.

Maharaj asks what we can learn even from Daksha's insults; a student answers that our mistakes are blamed on guru and Krishna. A disciple's acts go to the master, a citizen's to the king, so we must behave properly and be compassionate. — “people will see the organization”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:21 (auto-transcript): “the activities of the disciples goes to the special master the activities of the citizen goes to the king the activities of the workers goes to the proprietor so although daksha is speaking nonsensically but he has a good point that's a good point that we should behave…”

As Narada's followers are called breakers of families, ISKCON is opposed by caste brahmanas and worried parents, often out of envy. Maharaj says criticism means our work is being noticed; Krishna will recognise it, so we keep preaching unafraid.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:44 (auto-transcript): “I will say when people start criticizing will be recognized by Krishna and Krishna will give us blessings. But common people would recognize by criticizing. Why? Why? Why? Yes. Let us continue preaching the message of Lord Krishna and not be afraid of enemies. Our only duty…”

Maharaj agrees with Daksha on one point: changing dress, food, scripture and religion is not enough unless the heart changes. Renunciation must come from awakened knowledge. — “We should also change the heart.”

We have been chanting for years, so how does the heart change? Maharaj answers: rigid practice, chanting together with tapasya, as Srila Prabhupada taught. Knowledge then shows in character, gentleness and detachment.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:27 (auto-transcript): “Rigid practice. Rigid practice will change the heart. Not just chanting. Rigid chanting. He said he proper told us that what? Chanting should go along with tapasya. That's a rigid chanting, rigid practice. Then the heart will change. But Zapotty Daksa was correct in stating…”

Maharaj recalls confessing sins every weekend, taking communion on Sunday and repeating the same sins from Monday. Atonement and punishment fail because the heart is not purified; prisoners often come out more hardened. Only bhakti, especially the holy name, uproots the seed of sin for ever. — “The heart is not getting purified.”

🎙 Maharaj at 71:11 (auto-transcript): “the same thing the same thing i remember they were christened this on the weekend we go to the priest to confess, I did this, I did that, I did that. Then the priest will look, listen carefully that we are confessing. Then, okay, now your sins are forgiven. And on Sunday, we…”

Daksha boasts of his sacrifices as a vow-keeping householder, but Maharaj asks what value they have if the heart is not purified. Detachment comes only by the association and blessings of pure devotees like Narada, through the message of Mahaprabhu and Srila Prabhupada.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:57 (auto-transcript): “only by the association of pure devotees is then we can get detachment otherwise sanctification will continue cannot stop that is not this the solution yes 43 you have made me lose my sons once and now you have again done the same inauspicious thing therefore you are a dascal…”

Daksha curses Narada never to stay in one place, and Srila Prabhupada writes that he inherited the same curse from his disciples' parents. Maharaj smiles: we should all be cursed like this, to travel everywhere and preach.

children.topic: A curse taken as a blessing
children.note:
Narada simply says 'very well' and does not curse back. Maharaj says a devotee stays positive in every situation; he has no enemies and turns every negative into something positive, and he came only to deliver Daksha.

🎙 Maharaj at 97:39 (auto-transcript): “Yes, the behavior of Naradimoni is that he didn't take the cause of Daksha as sinful. He didn't take it as something bad. He accepted it as a blessing. That is how positive the devotees will be. Devotees will be always positive in every situation. Because if we are a devotee,…”

A preacher must be humbler than grass and more tolerant than a tree because he cannot live an easy-going life. Maharaj says many challenges mean our activities have been noticed; facing them happily, without complaint or grudge, is real advancement. — “Easy going life means no advancement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 101:03 (auto-transcript): “Easy going life means what? Easy going life. You cannot make advancement. Easy going life means no advancement. Peaceful life, we are satisfied. You cannot make advancement means no advancement. If it is making advancement, it's a lot of challenges. A lot of challenges means…”

Narada stayed to hear every harsh word so Daksha's anger would spend itself and he could repent, as Jagai and Madhai did before Nityananda. Maharaj notes the chance was given, but Daksha stayed in his offensive mood and lost the mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:36 (auto-transcript): “the morning has given the chance but he didn't take it he still remained in his offensive offensive behavior so in this way he didn't get what is available for him by the mercy of normal morning okay that is the end of chapter five now we go to chapter six the progeny or the…”

At Brahma's request Daksha now begets sixty daughters; Maharaj jokes that he chose daughters so Narada would not take his sons again. The daughters are given to Yamaraja, Kasyapa, the moon god and others.

children.topic: The moon god and Krishna's weddings
children.note:
The moon married twenty-seven daughters but was attached only to Rohini. Maharaj contrasts Krishna, who expanded Himself to perform 16,100 weddings in one day, each queen thinking she alone was married; we can claim to be God but cannot act like Him.

🎙 Maharaj at 108:47 (auto-transcript): “One God married 27 daughters. And he became attracted to one only. Which one? Rohini. Rohini. He couldn't handle the whole 27. Christian married how many? 16,000? One or eight. He was staying with only one. Christian was staying with all of them. among God who was not staying…”

The neglected wives complained, Daksha cursed the moon with disease, and the moon took shelter of Lord Shiva. Maharaj tells how, by Krishna's suggestion, Shiva kept one half of the moon on his head and the other went to Daksha, so the dispute ended without betraying a shelter.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:39 (auto-transcript): “The remaining 26 daughters went to Daksha and complained. Our husband is not taking care of us. we are just married in name only and that's her who is always always angry always angry became angry with one God and he went to him why are you not taking care of my daughters…”

Puffed up on his throne, Indra does not rise for his guru, and Brihaspati silently leaves. Maharaj asks the class for the lesson; they answer that opulence stole Indra's intelligence and respect for superiors.

In the spiritual world opulence has no side effects, but here it causes trouble. Maharaj recalls thieves who planned for four days to rob Nityananda Prabhu because His body was covered with ornaments; Daksha too despised Shiva for having no house, from pride in his power.

🎙 Maharaj at 135:51 (auto-transcript): “opulence is not desirable in the spiritual world opulences are desirable because there is no side effect. In our travel, all our opulences are not desirable. India has a problem here because of the opulence. It's affected by it. We have seen similar incidences. The money has…”

Srila Prabhupada had more opulence than many, yet did not fall because he used everything for Krishna and had no material desire. For a non-devotee everything material is punishment, like a crown that pushes him down. — “renunciation is not poverty”

🎙 Maharaj at 142:26 (auto-transcript): “why proper did not fall talk now say it boldly say it boldly why didn't he fall see all the way the world you go proper is there he has money that is not a common man's house he used everything for Krishna's he didn't consider himself pure devotees have no material desires…”

A king on his throne need not rise for everyone, but must rise for his guru, brahmanas and Vaishnavas. Maharaj explains that Romaharsana stayed seated when Lord Balarama entered, disgracing his own teacher, and was punished.

Narada visited Dvaraka to see how Krishna managed 16,108 queens; in palace after palace Krishna stood up and washed his feet until Narada said it was enough. Playing a householder, Krishna honoured a sannyasi, and we should follow that etiquette.

🎙 Maharaj at 155:03 (auto-transcript): “First example is Krishna himself, Narada Muni. But the Muni went to Dvaraka. But that was informed. Krishna had married 16,100 and this was. Let me go and see what is happening there. Let me go and see what is happening. How is he doing it? So Narada Muni came. The community…”

Leaders in ignorance and their blind followers are like passengers on a stone boat that must sink. Maharaj asks the class to find the strong word and says the whole world is sinking in fighting, crime and loss of dignity.

Maharaj mentions artificial intelligence and asks why we need it: what happened to the original? A devotee answers that maya has stolen it. Trying to live an artificial life against nature is itself a punishment. — “Are we finished with original intelligence?”

🎙 Maharaj at 163:29 (auto-transcript): “Now we have AI. Do you know civilization? AI means what? Artificial intelligence. Are we finished with original intelligence? Are we finished with original intelligence? Why are we going for the artificial one? What happened to the original? I don't know what I'm saying.…”

children.topic: Religion is a vehicle, not the goal
children.note:
The human body is a good boat, guru the captain and scripture the favourable wind. Maharaj says many religions treat religion itself as the goal, offend Krishna by calling Him formless, and so sit in stone boats; a boat must be made of wood to float and move.

🎙 Maharaj at 167:44 (auto-transcript): “The goal of life. Demons do not know that religion is a vehicle to take us to the destination. So this religious fighting, of course, it is not a religious fight. It is demons who have entered the religious circle and causing the problems, imperceptibly. So they are giving us…”
Indra resolves to bow at Brihaspati's feet without duplicity. Maharaj stresses that a disciple must never be a hypocrite or unfaithful to his guru, and must not let familiarity breed contempt.

Questions on groups who disrespect the guru yet seem to flourish, on blasphemous devotees in the ashram, and on Srila Prabhupada's wish for varnashrama.

🎙 Maharaj at 172:31 (auto-transcript): “One question, like Ritwiks, they disrespect so much and still they are flourishing, like Ritwiks, they disrespected spiritual master but still they are you know flourishing how to thank you understand thank you retweak uh it's repeated but they are making they're making…”

A devotee asks why the ritviks, who disrespect the spiritual master, still seem to make progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 172:31 (auto-transcript): “One question, like Ritwiks, they disrespect so much and still they are flourishing, like Ritwiks, they disrespected spiritual master but still they are you know flourishing how to thank you understand thank you retweak uh it's repeated but they are making they're making…”

Maharaj asks what progress is: money and numbers are not success; check the anxiety inside and the bhakti. Duryodhana, a prince who went to mock the Pandavas, ended up crying in the Gandharvas' net until Arjuna freed him; the Pandavas won with fewer armies. A pure devotee does not fight for power, as Narada did not fight Daksha.

🎙 Maharaj at 173:18 (auto-transcript): “What is progress? What is progress? You think money, that is success. I have a big example. That is success. Money, that is success. Devotees, that is success. How are the devotees functioning? Have you checked? So if I shave my teeth, that means I'm happy. Do you not? I'm…”

nodeData.topic: Class 2 · Austerity in Bhakti Can Give Krishna
nodeData.note: SB 6.4.44–6.5.30 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj completes the Lord's words to Daksha and shows why austerity is the first principle of spiritual life: Brahma, every acharya and the sons of Daksha gained strength through it, and today it means voluntarily giving up what is available, not starving. He contrasts Daksha's selfish blessing with Narada's purity, decodes Narada's ten riddles to the Hariasvas, and warns that only our own offences can make us leave Krishna consciousness. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The Lord tells Daksha that he too wants the whole world to be happy. Maharaj explains that the material world is set up as a chance for conditioned souls to get free, and that giving people Krishna consciousness is how a preacher becomes very dear to Krishna, which is why devotees take risks to do it.

Quoting Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Maharaj says our secondary nature has become primary. We are not material beings trying to become spiritual; the condition has become chronic, so even with scriptures, holy places, deities and devotees all around us, the cure takes time. — “We are spiritual beings who are undergoing material experience.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:44 (auto-transcript): “As Bhakti Mnathakura said, Bhakti Mnathakura said, our secondary nature has become primary. Our primary nature has become secondary. Therefore, many living entities think that we are material beings who are trying to become spiritual. It's a big ignorance. We are not material…”

The verse describes austerity, Vedic hymns, sacrifices and the demigods as the Lord's heart, body, limbs and life, a way for someone who cannot yet see God to perceive him. Maharaj stresses that tapasya comes first because it purifies.

As austerity clears the dirt from the heart, Krishna is revealed gradually, gradually, until one can see him face to face.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:20 (auto-transcript): “The first principle is Tapashya, which means denial of material activities. That's the first principle of spiritual life, because it brings purification. he explained that yesterday brings purification to the heart when all the coverings are removed it has become clear for…”

children.topic: The taste of water, even wine
children.note:
Gita 7.8 gives an impersonal way to begin seeing Krishna. Maharaj recalls Prabhupada's drastic remark that even a drinker who remembered the taste as Krishna would progress, though that is very rare: the acharyas go to any extent so no one can say they had no chance. Every mantra that begins with Om connects us to Krishna; only misfortune keeps us away.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:32 (auto-transcript): “But we get a location, say what? Start to see him, chapter 7. Chapter 7. I am the taste of water. No professor in the purple world. Remember? something like that and impersonal drinks then he just thinks that okay yes proper says something more very very drastic statement made”

Before creation the Lord existed with his own potencies, and the word 'aham' points to a person, not a void. Krishna never goes out of existence; whether he is manifest or unmanifest depends on our vision, not on him. From him came Brahma, the self-born.

Maharaj asks the class. Answers come: bhakti is personal, natural to the soul, conquers Krishna, and other paths need some bhakti to succeed. Karma and jnana carry selfishness and rely on our own strength; Mahaprabhu told Murari Gupta they darken the heart. Only bhakti, a loving relationship, has the potency to give prema.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:55 (auto-transcript): “Why bhakti yoga? What is so important in bhakti? What makes bhakti superior to other processes? What makes bhakti processes superior to other processes? There are different processes of self-realization. Why the part of bhakti is superior to others? What makes it so special?…”

children.topic: Who listens to a voice without form?
children.note:
Daksha saw a beautifully dressed person, not light. Maharaj asks who would keep sitting if they heard a voice but saw no speaker; maybe it is a ghost. Form shapes consciousness, and with form come activities and pleasure. — “Who will sit here?”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:28 (auto-transcript): “Daxa saw him as a person. He didn't see light. He didn't see void. How many of us will sit here? How many of us will continue to sit here? If we are hearing the voice and not seeing the person, who will sit here? Don't worry. Just sit down. Just sit down. And let's talk about…”

Brahma is Svayambhu, born without a mother, and Krishna says he is father and mother of all. Maharaj asks which pastime shows him as mother. Can we eat or sleep without a form? Krishna is the supreme person, Isvara, controlling everything at all times.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:20 (auto-transcript): “Yes, and both the father and the mother, how did he show that? How did Krishna prove his mother and father? We agree, his father, but how did he show that he is the mother, for all of us? Very good, very good. Mother maintains, what else? Mother maintains in many ways by…”
Brahma felt incapable of creating until the Lord advised him to perform austerities; by them he could produce helpers like Daksha.

Brahma only speculated, and speculation brings fear: he trembled when he touched the water. After tapasya, glorification of Krishna came spontaneously. Our own austerity is simple, almost one 'for lazy people', yet it can give us Krishna. — “nothing is possible without austerity.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:48 (auto-transcript): “Lord Brahma told himself, incapable. How did he become capable? Austerity. Kropar said, nothing is possible without austerity. Nothing, nothing is possible without austerity. Everything becomes possible by austerity. it could be whatever small or great not as a brahma's type…”

Maharaj asks whether any acharya skipped austerity. Prabhupada fainted from the sun in Delhi and Bombay while preaching and nearly left his body from seasickness. Only Vena took his position without austerity, and he failed and died.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:20 (auto-transcript): “Is there any one of our acharyas who did not do any austerity? Any of our acharyas? He didn't do any austerity? Just go to where they are? Anyone? A devotee observes that seniors built the facilities through hardship; now everything is set up, so what does austerity mean for us?

🎙 Maharaj at 53:11 (auto-transcript): “What Tapasya is important and we see that Acharya's lives and even we can see our many seniors who have initially built the facilities, they underwent a lot of austerities. When I came, it was like very peaceful for staying and for eating or for any other activities, it's all…”

Starvation is having nothing. Austerity is when everything is available and you deliberately give it up for something higher, for Krishna's pleasure. — “austerity is different from starvation”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:01 (auto-transcript): “or mean so that because it's very important here it is told thank you austerity does not mean there is nothing austerity doesn't mean there is nothing austerity is different from starvation starvation means there is nothing so what to do i have no alternative there's no food…”

When Maharaj joined, devotees ate twice a day, went out from ten till five without even water, slept on mats and never sat on chairs, yet life was sweeter than today. Time, place and circumstance change, but austerity is still needed.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:49 (auto-transcript): “So, it is true that the time we join the movement, we eat only two times in a day. There's no rice boga, there's no boga-rya, It's only in the morning, 10 o'clock, everyone outside, till 5 p.m. And outside, you cannot buy anything, you cannot take anything, not even water.…”

Austerity is for the intelligent, not an excuse on Janmashtami to skip the fast. Ekadasi reduces the body's demands and increases the soul's. If we practise nicely, appetite drops on its own, a sign of progress; complaints that fasting makes us ill are mostly the mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:38 (auto-transcript): “foolish people austerity is done by intelligent people who are very intelligent it knows what they are looking for and they know that to reduce the demands of the body which is the purpose of akadasy akadasy is to teach us to do what to reduce the demands of the body and…”

The Lord gives Daksha the daughter of Pancajana to beget children. Maharaj contrasts Daksha's austerity with Narada's, and notes that Krishna is only facilitating Daksha's selfish desire; it is not pure devotion.

In his previous life, the boy Narada walked past gardens of delicious fruit, sweet water and fearsome animals without taking anything, choosing a tree that supports meditation. After all that, the Lord told him he would not see him again in that life. Daksha faced no such tests.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:14 (auto-transcript): “very nice christian did not tell that the money also performed austerity heavily right more than what that said did the money did after leaving the sages yes yeah four months very severe very severe one um that side did not experience the challenges that the money had have…”

Maharaj tells of someone blessed by Lord Shiva with a young body, a beautiful wife and strength to enjoy: that is punishment, not a Gosvami's blessing. Daksha saw the Lord face to face but did not get to go home, while Narada saw him briefly and received everything; even demons like Narada. — “anything else is punishment”

Daksha begets ten thousand gentle, obedient sons, the Hariasvas, who go to Narayana-saras to do austerities. Maharaj says gentleness and obedience let them follow their father, a quality needed to do anything wonderful. Narada, seeing their purity, comes with enigmatic words.

Maharaj asks how this is possible; students suggest the Lord's blessing or Diti's sons. He says not to judge by our age: pigs bear a dozen at once, beings then had mystic power and acted by the mind, some were even born from trees.

children.topic: Guru rewards the quality of practice
children.note:
Narada saw how high their austerity was and gave them ten subjects to ponder, as he gave an allegory to Pracinabarhi. A spiritual master watches the quality of a disciple's practice and rewards it. Maharaj notes Prabhupada opened temples in Mayapur and Vrindavan so devotees can bathe in Ganga and Yamuna.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:09 (auto-transcript): “seen the level of the austerity they are performing and he saw that the quality of the austerity is very, very high that just just a moment after this you become good devotees. Whoever Narada looks upon becomes a devotee, and he passes this potency to disciples like Prahlada. Only a few, such as Daksha and Kamsa, resisted even repeated visits. — “His mercy is unlimited.”

🎙 Maharaj at 99:27 (auto-transcript): “This is Narada Muni's mercy. His mercy is unlimited. that the demonic glance is so auspicious that whomever he glances upon must certainly become a devotee. Anyone who a demonic glance upon must surely become a devotee. That is his potency. And he transferred that energy to…”

How does this relate to me, how is the Lord connected, and how does it touch other living entities? From Daksha we learn not to waste life on sense gratification; the Lord used his desire in his service. Narada first 'breaks the ice' by asking whether they really know their father's order, capturing their minds. The Hariasvas then decode each riddle themselves: the earth is the body, the one man is Krishna, the hole is the spiritual world, the woman is unsteady intelligence, the swan is scripture, the razor wheel is time.

children.topic: Use this body for a spiritual one

On the swan of scripture, Maharaj says ISKCON has a great duty that scientists, politicians and philosophers cannot fulfil, because Krishna consciousness is the eternal culture of the soul; every other culture ends with the body.

children.topic: Mistakes are forgiven, not deliberate offences

If we keep sixteen rounds and the four principles and slip because of conditioning, Krishna forgives and we learn. Deliberate acts are what block us; when we notice an offence, sincerely beg forgiveness and continue.

nodeData.note: SB 6.4.1–43 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens SB 6.4 with the Pracetas, whose austerity left them angry, and Soma's plea for the trees, teaching that true knowledge and pure austerity soften the heart and that every body is a temple of the Lord. Through Daksha's Hamsa-guhya prayers he stresses that Krishna is reached by the attitude of service, not speculation, and explains why there are so many philosophies and religions: Krishna gives each person what he desires and level by level draws all toward himself. children.topic: A guru's fire passes to the ripe
children.note:
Narada's words so affected King Pracinabarhi that he could not wait to leave for the forest. Maharaj explains that a bona fide master always transforms a ripe disciple, passing on the fire of bhakti he himself received from the sages; if the disciple is not ripe, nothing happens.

Maharaj presses the class: Prabhupada says a devotee is never angry, yet he and other masters chastised disciples strongly. The answer: it only looks like anger in our language. children.topic: What is in the heart transfers

Angry people cannot preach, for every pure devotee, even the Lord himself, was harassed by those he came to help. The moon-deity Soma, maintainer of all plants, sees the trees burning and pacifies the Pracetas with sympathy. Maharaj asks how the moon maintains vegetation: he places the six tastes in plants, giving us fruits, flowers, vegetables and oxygen.

children.note:

Soma reminds the Pracetas that a king must wish his citizens prosperity and protect them. Maharaj adds Prabhupada's point that a citizen is anyone born in the land, so animals and trees are citizens too and must be protected, not killed. — “That means that animals are also citizens.”

children.topic: A cow's hairs, a cow's milk
children.note:
Who could count the hairs on one cow? Maharaj says killing a cow keeps us bound for that many years, one reason we stay so long in this world. We drink our mother's milk for some months but cow's milk for a lifetime, so the cow is more our mother and must be protected.

The class began late because everyone ate a heavy feast after fasting and fell asleep. Maharaj uses it to teach sense control: break a fast lightly and gradually, and do not listen to the mind, which says you are tired when you are only full. — “because the mind is not a devotee”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:26 (auto-transcript): “what what was the reason what the reason for coming late eating heavy fists eating heavy fists you know when you fast and then you eat heavy what will happen to the body the body will be weak the body will be really weak so we cannot control the senses like that we cannot…”

Sense control begins not with the tongue but with the mind, the master of all the senses; control the mind and the rest follow. Maharaj explains that although intelligence should guide the mind, the mind is often strong enough to overpower it.
