The verse asks us to see every body as a residence of the Lord. Maharaj says unity in diversity can never come until this is realised: if I do not see the Lord living in you, I will not value you and will naturally misuse you. — “If we want to have unity and diversity, then this should be realized.”

Real knowledge from a self-realised soul shows that all living beings belong to Krishna. Maharaj says such knowledge changes how we relate to and treat everything, and it makes one humble; that is why pure devotees respect all.

The verse praises one who subdues sudden anger. Devotees ask daily how to control lust and anger; Maharaj says tolerance depends on inner strength, which comes from purity, not from philosophy, just as only a well-prepared student passes. We should measure our progress by how much we can tolerate, as a traveller must know the distance to set his speed.

Soma offers the Pracetas Marisa as their wife to pacify them. Maharaj compares Hiranyakasipu, whose meditation was broken by anger after Narada chanted; he went home to his wife, Prahlada was conceived, and he returned to his austerities.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:29 (auto-transcript): “how did he control it the money came to him and chanted my enemy became angry with that contamination he cannot control meditation so what did he do he came back to the house and he slept with his wife that is how he anger was removed they control the anger and that is how…”

Marisa's mother Pramloca was no ordinary apsara. Maharaj tells how two demon brothers won a boon that only they could kill each other; Vishnu gathered beauty from everything to form Pramloca, and the brothers quarrelled over her until they killed each other.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:12 (auto-transcript): “From Rocha is as is mentioned in Absara is not the Absara like we get in the heavenly planet. From Rocha came from Krishna himself because after Hirakasipu was killed along with some others. There's some who fled out of fear on the second day. So, those who fled, they went to…”

Daksha means expert, a quality of a Vaishnava, but Maharaj notes this Daksha is expert for sense gratification. Having offended Lord Shiva, he once received a goat's head, and the same Daksha is now born again of the Pracetas.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:13 (auto-transcript): “one of the qualities of vajshanma is daksha so this is daksha here is that quality this is daksha here is that quality when this is quality for vajshanma daksha which one is this which one is this this one is sanctification daksha it's part for sanctification not that it has…”

Daksha's Hamsa-guhya prayers were not his own composition but already existed in Vedic literature. Maharaj asks why: Daksha, materially motivated, lacked the purity to compose such a prayer from his heart, yet the prayer was so potent that the Lord was pleased and appeared.

Understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very difficult, which is why few follow this path. Maharaj says only the extremely fortunate take to Krishna consciousness, where service makes one's existence pure.

All the coverings on our consciousness are removed by the attitude of service. Maharaj recalls Prabhupada's saying that advancement depends on the attitude of the follower.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:15 (auto-transcript): “The Lord can be realized by the attitude of service. The attitude of service. All these coverings in our consciousness can be removed completely by our service attitude. And the famous quote from Prabhupada's instruction, famous quote, famous advancement”

Kamsa and Sisupala thought of Krishna day and night, the very absorption we struggle for, yet their meditation is condemned because their attitude was demonic. Krishna already has everything; what he values is our attitude. — “Even when he's sleeping, he thinks of Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:20 (auto-transcript): “Okay, for example, Kamsa was 24 hours Krishna conscious. What was wrong with his meditation? Kamsa, unfavorable, unfavorable attitude. Sissupal, think of Krishna 24 hours. Sissupal. Kamsa, he think of Krishna 24 hours. What is wrong with your meditation? Something which we…”

Maharaj tells the Bible story of a poor woman who gave her only coin while others gave fortunes; Jesus held up her gift as the purest he had received. She gave everything without thinking of tomorrow; a gift given condescendingly is no gift at all.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:01 (auto-transcript): “There is a story like that in a Bible. there is a story like that in the bible jesus was in the church and thousands of followers are there and they were giving him amount of money they were giving so much there was a lady one lady in her entire life she has only one rupee…”

On one sankirtana day one devotee distributed five books and Maharaj forty-five, yet the five-book devotee was glorified. Maharaj, feeling slighted, was told the other devotee had put in more effort and so received more purification. — “the energy he put into this is more than the energy”

🎙 Maharaj at 92:38 (auto-transcript): “one day we we went on Sankita one devotee distributed only five books and one other god brother he distributed more than us he did 45 books one did five when the resolve was announced grudel was glorifying the one who gave who distributed five books and the one who did 45…”

The verse places the Lord beyond everything expressed by material sound, mind or senses. Maharaj says Krishna exists before, during and after creation and is reached only by his causeless mercy when senses, mind and intelligence are engaged in service with the right attitude, beginning with the tongue.

The verse says the Lord, from within, keeps speculators agreeing and disagreeing without conclusion. Maharaj asks why Krishna does this: because they want to forget him, he gives them ample reason to forget, just as he gives devotees reason to remember. It is not his fault but his nature. — “He's doing it by our desire.”

Those who do not want Krishna get thousands of subjects to discuss. Maharaj points to endless cell-phone and car models that only change name and colour and keep us anxious; no phone can reach Krishna, but the tongue he gave us can. — “Only our tongue has to call that Krishna direct number.”

🎙 Maharaj at 109:02 (auto-transcript): “how many varieties of cell phone we have how many varieties cell phone yeah thousands because I use the word so thousands of subjects simple what is it what is it useful yourself what did you use common useful is make a call and receive a call right so then we're having…”

If God is one, why so many religions? Because people are at different levels, Krishna lovingly provides for each, like kindergarten, primary school, college and research. We also came through that speculation over many lifetimes, so being a devotee is great fortune; Prabhupada wrote to one devotee not to take the process cheaply. — “we should not take it cheaply”

🎙 Maharaj at 114:13 (auto-transcript): “this is one side that is just one side what are the other reasons if the absolute is one if god is one why soon the religion why why so the religion if god is one because everybody is not uh is not on that level to understand everybody is on a different level therefore there…”

Sankhya and bhakti both point to the same ultimate cause, but the analyst goes the long way round, counting elements, and few arrive. Maharaj says even the royal road of bhakti has accidents, and the rough road far more, so it is fortune to take to Krishna consciousness.

Krishna consciousness is the most difficult thing in the world: a degree takes five years, but how many lives to graduate as a devotee? Prabhupada and his guru wanted disciples to go back this life; Prabhupada's purports explain that most do not really want to go back. Krishna has opened the gate; it depends on us.

🎙 Maharaj at 121:41 (auto-transcript): “to take to christian consciousness in fact the most difficult thing for anyone to do in this world is is the most difficult thing one can ever do in life christian consciousness it's christian consciousness go to any college after five years we are graduate is it not how many…”
Is the Lord partial to devotees? Maharaj says no: those who worship him as a person see him as a person, and those who deny his form get no form. His names, form and pastimes are not material.

Impersonalists think any form must be defective like ours, so they treat deities as a means to be thrown away later; Maharaj says formlessness comes from frustration. A prison commissioner who visits a prison does not become a prisoner; his visit brings amnesty, just as Krishna's coming lets us see and hear him. — “formlessness is due to frustration”

🎙 Maharaj at 132:25 (auto-transcript): “they think that there is so much problem in name and form here so if lord also has form and name that means so all forms in this this world has some defect they are conditioned so if the lord has form he also become a conditioned person conditioned soul that is their…”

The Lord's name is not material: Ajamila called his son Narayana, and Narayana responded to his own name and delivered him.

🎙 Maharaj at 135:50 (auto-transcript): “And his name is not material like the proper said. Just calling Narayan, he got liberated. Even though he was not calling Narayan. But Narayan says, my name is calling. Let me do something. Let me do something. And he got what he did again. Because in the name of the Lord is…”

The verse compares the Lord's appearance through lower forms of worship to air carrying a fragrance. Maharaj says the Lord reveals himself only by his grace, not by speculation; the devotee's prayer is to see him as he actually is.

The Lord appears on Garuda with eight arms, ornaments and his associates. Maharaj insists these ornaments are no imagination; seeing Jagannatha or Radha-Krishna decorated every day, devotees have the great fortune of serving the Lord in person.

Daksha falls flat like a rod, as Dhruva did in another age; the same response in different ages shows it is real. Maharaj cites the saying that the eye that sees God shall die: one is transformed, as Dhruva no longer wanted the kingdom he came for. Losing taste for old attractions is the sign of advancement. — “you can never be the same person again”
